text:
The son will most likely **lose**. An intended beneficiary's rights vest only when he relies on the contract, manifests assent at the parties' request, or sues, and he had done none of these before the landscaper and owner agreed to redirect payment to the father, so the owner's payment to the father discharged the owner's duty. The shared note is wrong: under Restatement (Second) of Contracts § 311, rights do not vest automatically at signing, so the parties could still change the payee. The main risk to the owner's defense is a challenge that the redirection lacked consideration, since the owner's payment amount did not change.

CONFIDENCE: 70
